gaps: normals: this node draws the analytic normal dS/du x dS/dv at every grid point; X_ITE 16.6.0 averages face normals inside an 85 degree crease, so at low tessellation its shading is faceted where ours is smooth (measured largest component difference 0.21 at 12 x 12 cells and 0.28 at 8 x 8, compared at 0.3)
weights: X_ITE 16.6.0 does not apply them as a rational surface needs (the quarter cylinder reaches radius 1.24); this node follows the standard (radius 1 to 1e-5), checked in this engine only

solid FALSE seen from behind: X_ITE 16.6.0 lights the back face, the Babylon body draws a counter-clockwise face seen from behind black (the same for an IndexedFaceSet with solid FALSE, measured in a two-quad fixture: 9312 against 19012 drawn pixels); the patch P6 is therefore off screen and only its triangles are compared

a closed surface (uClosed): positions, texture coordinates and the triangles agree with X_ITE; the shading is smooth across the seam here, X_ITE leaves a seam in its normals (its own source says "TODO: handle uClosed")
NurbsTextureCoordinate as texCoord is a later batch (a TextureCoordinate with one point per control point is supported and compared)
scope: triangle corners, texture coordinates and normals come from the vertex arrays X_ITE builds (private getVertices, getMultiTexCoords, getNormals) and from the mesh this reader builds; the pictures are silhouette and mean colour (SwiftShader CPU raster, no tone curve)
